newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer Medica bookbuilding starts June 30.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer Medica bookbuilding starts June 30.

text.p: Sulzer AG said bookbuilding for its Sulzer Medica unit's public share offering would start on June 30 and that shareholders would get the right to buy one Medica share for every 10 Sulzer shares they own as of June 27.

The offering of shares in Sulzer Medica, a medical technology company, will comprise 2.3 million new shares to be listed on both the Swiss Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange, in the form of American depository shares.
"Trading is expected to commence in the week of July 14, 1997," it said in a statement. Sulzer chief executive Fritz Fahrni will be chairman of Sulzer Medica.
"As a result of the offering, approximately 24 percent of the share capital in Sulzer Medica will be held by the public, with the rest remaining with Sulzer AG," it said.
Sulzer AG shareholders will be allowed to take part in an advance subscription offering fron June 30 to July 9.

"This offering gives each Sulzer AG shareholder the non-tradeable right to purchase one Sulzer Medica share at the offering price for every 10 Sulzer AG shares held on June 27, 1997," it said. It did not give any pricing indication.
All proceeds will go to Sulzer Medica to support its pursuit of growth opportunities, it said.
Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is global coordinator. SBC Warburg is co-global coordinator. Underwriters have the option to buy an extra 300,000 shares to cover any overallotment.
Sulzer Medica, now wholly owned by Sulzer, posted 1.16 billion Swiss francs in 1996 sales and employed 4,557 people.

It designs, manufactures and markets a range of implantable orthopedic and cardiovascular products. Orthopedic products accounted for 52 percent and cardiovascular products for 48 percent of 1996 sales. Europe made up 47 percent of sales and North America 40 percent.
Its board will include existing Sulzer board members Pierre Borgeaud, Peter Spaelti and Reto Domeniconi as well as Max Link and Larry Mathis, it said.
